title: 二十四把椅子刚刚好  (Twenty-Four Chairs After All)

segments.t: At a quarter to six under warm courtyard lanterns, Qing and Hao are setting out teacups when Manager Zhou rushes back from the open street gate wide-eyed. Listen first.
小晴！志豪！快来看我们大门外的人行道！
才五点四十五分——大家已经到了吗？！
书店老板、药店药剂师、面包师的表弟，还有十二位邻居！
九号房里面的十二把椅子，三分钟就全坐满了！
等等——院子拱门底下那十二把备用的折叠椅呢？！
就是我星期六不小心订错的那一批吗？！
快把十二把全打开，摆在院子里的四张木桌旁边！
周经理，你那二十四把特价椅子，每一把都有客人坐啦！
小晴，你听见了吗？！我的失误其实是天才的商业计划！
周经理，快鞠个躬，笑着把菜单卡片发给大家吧！
把拱窗大大地打开，让大树底下的人都听见钢琴声！
欢迎，朋友们，欢迎！热薄荷茶马上就端出来！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
小晴！志豪！快来看我们大门外的人行道！
'Qing! Hao! Come look at the pavement outside our main gate!' Mandarin's word for pavement, "renxingdao", spells out its job in three transparent blocks: "person-walk-path".
才五点四十五分——大家已经到了吗？！
'It is only a quarter to six—are people arriving already?!' Tiny "cai" right before the time means "only five forty-five", signalling straight away that the crowd is much earlier than Qing expected.
书店老板、药店药剂师、面包师的表弟，还有十二位邻居！

'The bookshop owner, the pharmacist, the baker's cousin, and twelve neighbours!' Zhou counts people with polite "wei" in true host fashion. And unlike English "cousin", "biaodi" tells you it is specifically a younger male cousin on the mother's or aunt's side.
九号房里面的十二把椅子，三分钟就全坐满了！

'All twelve chairs inside Room Nine just filled up in three minutes!' Pair Qing's earlier "cai" with Hao's "jiu" here: right after "three minutes", "jiu" means "that fast!". And "zuo man" literally says "sat full".
等等——院子拱门底下那十二把备用的折叠椅呢？！

'Wait—what about those twelve extra folding chairs under the courtyard arch?!' Dropping tiny "ne" onto the end of a thing turns "those twelve spare folding chairs" into a quick "what about...?" question.
就是我星期六不小心订错的那一批吗？！

'The ones I ordered by mistake on Saturday?!' Snapping "cuo", "wrong", onto "ding", "order", gives "dingcuo"—ordered wrong. You can attach "cuo" to almost any everyday action: hear wrong, write wrong, or grab the wrong suitcase.
快把十二把全打开，摆在院子里的四张木桌旁边！

'Unfold all twelve around the four outdoor courtyard tables right now!' Hear two different jobs for "ba" in one breath: the first "ba" tees up what Hao is acting on, while the second "ba" counts the twelve chairs.
周经理，你那二十四把特价椅子，每一把都有客人坐啦！

'Every single one of your twenty-four bargain chairs has a guest, Manager Zhou!' "Tejia" shrinks "special price" into two crisp shop-sign syllables for "bargain" or "on sale", and "mei yi ba dou" emphasizes every single chair without exception.
小晴，你听见了吗？！我的失误其实是天才的商业计划！

'Did you hear that, Qing?! My mistake was actually a brilliant business plan!' Zhou happily rewrites history with "qishi", "actually", and calls his plan "tiancai"—literally "heaven-sent talent", a genius stroke.
周经理，快鞠个躬，笑着把菜单卡片发给大家吧！

'Take a bow, Manager Zhou, and hand out the menu cards with a smile!' "Jugong", "to bow", splits right down the middle in casual speech so "ge" slips inside—"ju ge gong"—just like English "take a bow".
把拱窗大大地打开，让大树底下的人都听见钢琴声！

'Open the arched windows wide so everyone under the tree hears the piano!' Doubling "big" into "dada de" turns it into "wide open", and "rang", literally "let", smoothly links an action to what it makes possible.
欢迎，朋友们，欢迎！热薄荷茶马上就端出来！

'Welcome, friends, welcome! Hot mint tea is coming right out!' "Mashang" literally means "on horseback"—centuries ago, that was as fast as anything could arrive, and today it means "coming right out!".
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
小晴！志豪！快来看我们大门外的人行道！
才五点四十五分——大家已经到了吗？！
书店老板、药店药剂师、面包师的表弟，还有十二位邻居！
九号房里面的十二把椅子，三分钟就全坐满了！
等等——院子拱门底下那十二把备用的折叠椅呢？！
就是我星期六不小心订错的那一批吗？！
快把十二把全打开，摆在院子里的四张木桌旁边！
周经理，你那二十四把特价椅子，每一把都有客人坐啦！
小晴，你听见了吗？！我的失误其实是天才的商业计划！
周经理，快鞠个躬，笑着把菜单卡片发给大家吧！
把拱窗大大地打开，让大树底下的人都听见钢琴声！
欢迎，朋友们，欢迎！热薄荷茶马上就端出来！
Every single one of Manager Zhou's twenty-four bargain chairs fills with smiling neighbours under the courtyard lanterns! See you next time.
下次见！
